definition: Analog-to-Digital Converter; converts a voltage from a sensor into a digital number a microcontroller can process.
Annualized Loss Expectancy; expected yearly financial loss, calculated as SLE × ARO.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing; slash notation such as /24 that describes an IP network prefix length.
Digital Multimeter; measures voltage, resistance, continuity, and—in the correct series configuration—current.
Endpoint Detection and Response; endpoint telemetry and response tooling used to detect, investigate, and contain suspicious behavior.
Electrostatic Discharge; a sudden static-electricity transfer that can damage sensitive electronic components.
Kirchhoff's Current Law; total current entering a node equals total current leaving it.
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law; the algebraic sum of voltage rises and drops around a closed loop is zero.
Multi-Factor Authentication; authentication using two or more independent factor types such as knowledge, possession, or inherence.
Network Access Control; controls network admission based on identity, device state, or policy—often through 802.1X.
Public Key Infrastructure; certificate authorities, certificates, policies, and processes that bind public keys to identities.
Pulse Width Modulation; rapidly switches a digital signal on and off to control average power or approximate an analog output.
Recovery Point Objective; the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured in time.
Recovery Time Objective; the maximum acceptable downtime after an outage.
Security Information and Event Management; centralizes, normalizes, correlates, and alerts on security telemetry.
Single Loss Expectancy; the cost of one loss event, calculated as asset value × exposure factor.
Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response; coordinates approved response workflows across security tools.
Virtual Local Area Network; a logical Layer 2 network segment and separate broadcast domain on shared switch infrastructure.
A security model that continuously verifies identity, device posture, context, and least privilege rather than trusting network location.
